a, b and c are real numbers with a < b < c.
Column A: (a + c)/2
Column B: b
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation:
Column A is the midpoint of the two OUTER numbers. Column B is the middle number, which the stem only requires to lie somewhere between a and c - anywhere at all.
Case 1 — b sits exactly halfway: a = 1, b = 2, c = 3. Column A = (1 + 3)/2 = 2 = Column B. Equal.
Case 2 — b hugs the left end: a = 1, b = 2, c = 10. Column A = 5.5, Column B = 2. Column A greater.
Case 3 — b hugs the right end: a = 1, b = 9, c = 10. Column A = 5.5, Column B = 9. Column B greater.
All three outcomes occur, so no relationship holds in general.
Answer: D.
questions.trap: Choosing C on the feeling that 'b is in the middle, so b is the average'. Being between two numbers and being their midpoint are different conditions: b is pinned only by two inequalities, while the midpoint is pinned by an equation. Sliding b toward either end while holding a and c fixed breaks the tie in either direction, which is precisely what makes the answer D.

questions.question: On the number line, point X is three times as far from -2 as it is from 6. What is the sum of all possible coordinates of X? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — write the condition with distances: |x + 2| = 3|x - 6|.
Step 2 — an absolute-value equation splits into two cases.
Case 1, same sign: x + 2 = 3(x - 6) gives x + 2 = 3x - 18, so 2x = 20 and x = 10.
Case 2, opposite sign: x + 2 = -3(x - 6) gives x + 2 = -3x + 18, so 4x = 16 and x = 4.
Step 3 — verify both against the original distances.
x = 10: distance to -2 is 12, distance to 6 is 4, and 12 = 3(4). Valid.
x = 4: distance to -2 is 6, distance to 6 is 2, and 6 = 3(2). Valid.
Step 4 — sum: 10 + 4 = 14.
Why there are two: one solution sits INSIDE the segment from -2 to 6, where the two distances split the gap 3 : 1; the other sits OUTSIDE, to the right of 6, where moving away from both points keeps the 3 : 1 ratio.
Answer: 14.
questions.trap: Finding only the interior point x = 4 - by splitting the 8-unit gap in the ratio 3 : 1 - and answering 4. The condition never says X lies between the two points, and the exterior solution x = 10 satisfies it just as well. The other error is reversing the ratio and putting X three times as far from 6 as from -2, which gives x = 0 and x = -6.

questions.question:
a and b are real numbers with a < 0 < b. Consider the seven values a, b, a + b, a - b, ab, a/b, b/a. Which of the following must be true?
I. The seven values include both a positive and a negative value.
II. The median of the seven values is positive.
III. a/b and b/a have opposite signs.
options: E. None of I, II and III must be true.
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — sign each of the seven values.
a: negative (given).
b: positive (given).
a - b: negative minus positive, so negative.
ab: negative times positive, so negative.
a/b: negative over positive, so negative.
b/a: positive over negative, so negative.
a + b: sign unknown - it depends on which of |a| and b is larger.
So five values are certainly negative, one is certainly positive, and one is unknown.
Step 2 — statement I. a is negative and b is positive, so both signs are present no matter what. TRUE.
Step 3 — statement II. With seven values the median is the 4th smallest. At least five of them are negative, so positions 1 through 5 in sorted order are all negative, and the 4th is among them. The median is therefore negative, never positive. FALSE.
Step 4 — statement III. a/b is negative and b/a is negative - a quotient and its reciprocal always share a sign. They are both negative, so they do NOT have opposite signs. FALSE.
Only I must be true.
Check with a = -1, b = 4: the values are -1, 4, 3, -5, -4, -0.25, -4. Sorted: -5, -4, -4, -1, -0.25, 3, 4. Median = -1, negative, and both quotients are negative. Consistent.
Answer: A.
questions.trap: Statement III is the bait: a and b have opposite signs, so students transfer that to their quotients. Reciprocals never flip sign - if a/b is negative, so is b/a. Statement II fails for a counting reason people skip: you must notice that FIVE of the seven values are forced negative, which pins the 4th smallest below zero regardless of where a + b lands. Answering C or B costs the question.

questions.question:
x and y are non-zero real numbers with xy < 0 and x + y > 0.
Column A: |x + y|
Column B: |x| + |y|
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — read the conditions. xy < 0 says x and y have OPPOSITE signs. x + y > 0 says the positive one has the larger magnitude.
Step 2 — take x > 0 and y < 0 (the other case is the same with the letters swapped).
Column A = |x + y| = x + y, since the sum is positive.
Column B = |x| + |y| = x + (-y) = x - y, since |y| = -y for negative y.
Step 3 — subtract: Column B - Column A = (x - y) - (x + y) = -2y. Because y < 0, -2y > 0.
So Column B exceeds Column A by exactly 2|y|, which is strictly positive since y is non-zero.
Check across different magnitudes:
x = 5, y = -1: Column A = 4, Column B = 6.
x = 5, y = -4.9: Column A = 0.1, Column B = 9.9.
x = 100, y = -0.01: Column A = 99.99, Column B = 100.01.
Column B is greater every time.
Answer: B.
questions.trap: Recognising the triangle inequality |x + y| <= |x| + |y| and settling on C because equality is the familiar case. Equality holds only when x and y point the SAME way; here xy < 0 forces opposite directions, so the inequality is strict and B wins. The gap can be made as small as you like (the third check gives 0.02) but it is never zero, which is exactly why the answer is B and not D.

questions.question: Let f(x) = |x - 3| + |x + 2|. For which of the following values of x does f(x) attain its minimum value? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — read f as a total distance: |x - 3| is the distance from x to 3, and |x + 2| is the distance from x to -2. So f(x) is the combined distance from x to the two fixed points -2 and 3.
Step 2 — the two points are |3 - (-2)| = 5 apart. Any x BETWEEN them splits that 5 into two pieces that add back to 5. Any x outside overshoots one point and then has to come back, so the total exceeds 5.
Step 3 — confirm algebraically by region.
For -2 <= x <= 3: f(x) = (3 - x) + (x + 2) = 5, a constant - the x cancels.
For x > 3: f(x) = (x - 3) + (x + 2) = 2x - 1 > 5.
For x < -2: f(x) = (3 - x) + (-x - 2) = 1 - 2x > 5.
The minimum value is 5, attained on the whole closed interval [-2, 3].
Step 4 — test the options.
A - x = -5: f = 8 + 3 = 11. Not minimal. FALSE.
B - x = -2: f = 5 + 0 = 5. Minimal. TRUE.
C - x = 0: f = 3 + 2 = 5. Minimal. TRUE.
D - x = 3: f = 0 + 5 = 5. Minimal. TRUE.
E - x = 6: f = 3 + 8 = 11. Not minimal. FALSE.
Answer: B, C, D.
questions.trap: Assuming the minimum happens at one special point - usually the midpoint 0.5 - and selecting only the option nearest it. A sum of two distances is flat across the entire segment joining the two anchors, so infinitely many x tie for the minimum, endpoints included. The second error is excluding the endpoints B and D on the grounds that one distance becomes 0 there; a distance of 0 is allowed, and 5 + 0 is still 5.

questions.question: Which of the following is equal to 10^0?
questions.explanation: Any nonzero number raised to the power of 0 equals 1. Therefore 10^0 = 1. This is a fundamental exponent rule: x^0 = 1 for all x ≠ 0.
questions.trap: Students choose A (0) because they think 'zero exponent means zero'. The exponent 0 means the number is divided by itself once (10^1 / 10^1 = 10/10 = 1), not that the result is 0.

questions.question: What is 3.7 × 10^3 expressed in standard form?
questions.explanation: To convert from scientific notation to standard form, move the decimal point to the right by the number of places indicated by the exponent. 10^3 means move the decimal 3 places to the right: 3.7 → 37. → 370. → 3700. So 3.7 × 10^3 = 3,700.
questions.trap: Students choose B (370) by moving the decimal only 2 places instead of 3, or they confuse the exponent with the number of zeros to append rather than the number of decimal places to shift.

questions.question: What is the value of 10^(-2)?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — read the negative exponent as a reciprocal, not as a sign: 10^(-n) = 1/10^n.
Step 2 — 10^(-2) = 1/10^2 = 1/100 = 0.01.
Step 3 — sanity check the sign of the exponent. A negative exponent always produces a number between 0 and 1, never a negative number.
Answer: 0.01.
questions.trap: Choosing -100, which comes from carrying the minus sign into the value instead of into the exponent. Choice B, -0.01, is the half-corrected version: reciprocal taken but the sign kept. Choice E, 0.1, moves the decimal point only one place instead of two.

questions.question: The number 0.00056 is written in scientific notation as a x 10^n, where 1 <= a < 10. What is the value of n? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — find the coefficient. The decimal point must land just after the first nonzero digit, so a = 5.6.
Step 2 — count the places moved. Going from 0.00056 to 5.6 moves the point 4 places to the RIGHT.
Step 3 — moving right makes the coefficient bigger, so the exponent must shrink to compensate: n = -4.
Check: 5.6 x 10^(-4) = 5.6/10000 = 0.00056. Correct.
Answer: -4.
questions.trap: Answering 4. The number is less than 1, so its exponent must be negative - a positive exponent would make 5.6 x 10^4 = 56,000. A second slip is answering -3 by counting only the zeros after the decimal point (three) instead of counting all the way to the first nonzero digit (four places).

questions.question: Which of the following expresses 45,000 in correct scientific notation?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — correct scientific notation is a x 10^k with the coefficient a satisfying 1 <= a < 10 and k an integer. Place the decimal point to meet that rule: a = 4.5.
Step 2 — count places from 4.5 to 45,000: 4.5 -> 45 -> 450 -> 4,500 -> 45,000, four places to the left, so the exponent is 4.
Step 3 — 45,000 = 4.5 x 10^4.
Check: 4.5 x 10,000 = 45,000. Correct. Note that A (45) and D (0.45) also equal 45,000 but violate 1 <= a < 10, so neither is correct scientific notation.
questions.trap: Choices A and D are both numerically equal to 45,000 but neither is scientific notation: 45 is not less than 10 and 0.45 is not at least 1. Answer choices are always in proper standard form, so a coefficient outside [1, 10) is automatically wrong. Choice B, 4.5 x 10^3 = 4,500, moves the point one place too few; choice E, 4.5 x 10^5 = 450,000, one place too many.

questions.question:
Column A: 10^4
Column B: 4^10
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.trap: Students see the same two digits (10 and 4) and assume the one with the larger base (10^4) must be larger. They reverse the base and exponent, ignoring the dramatic effect of a large exponent on a moderate base.

questions.question: What is 10^5 × 10^3?
questions.explanation: When multiplying powers with the same base, add the exponents: 10^5 × 10^3 = 10^(5+3) = 10^8.
questions.trap: Students choose B (10^15) by multiplying the exponents instead of adding them. The rule 'multiply exponents' applies to a power of a power (10^5)^3, not to a product of same-base powers.

questions.question: What is 10^6 ÷ 10^4?
questions.explanation: When dividing powers with the same base, subtract the exponents: 10^6 ÷ 10^4 = 10^(6-4) = 10^2 = 100.
questions.trap: Students compute 10^(6÷4) = 10^1.5 by dividing the exponents instead of subtracting them. The division rule for same-base exponents is subtraction, not division.

questions.question: The population of a city is approximately 2.4 x 10^6. Which of the following is this population written out in full?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — a positive exponent moves the decimal point to the RIGHT, one place per unit of the exponent.
Step 2 — move the point in 2.4 six places right: 24 -> 240 -> 2,400 -> 24,000 -> 240,000 -> 2,400,000.
Step 3 — as a place-value check, 10^6 is one million, so 2.4 x 10^6 is 2.4 million = 2,400,000.
Answer: 2,400,000.
questions.trap: Choosing 240,000, which is 2.4 x 10^5 - the point was moved five places, not six. Choice C comes from appending six zeros to the digits '24' instead of moving the point six places from 2.4. Choice E moves the point in the wrong direction, which would require a negative exponent.

questions.question: Which of the following are equal to 0.001? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation:
First fix the target: 0.001 = 1/1000 = 10^(-3).
A - 10^(-3) is exactly the target. TRUE.
B - 1/10^3 = 1/1000 = 0.001. This is the definition of a negative exponent, so it is the same object as A. TRUE.
C - multiplying powers of the same base ADDS exponents: 10^(-1) x 10^(-2) = 10^(-1 + -2) = 10^(-3) = 0.001. TRUE.
D - this is addition, so exponents do not combine: 0.1 + 0.01 = 0.11. FALSE.
E - 1/10^(-3) = 10^3 = 1000, because dividing by 10^(-3) is multiplying by 10^3. FALSE.
Answer: A, B, C.
questions.trap: D is the live bait: students who have just learned that 10^(-1) x 10^(-2) = 10^(-3) apply the same move to a plus sign and get 0.001 again, when the true value is 0.11. E punishes the opposite carelessness - a reciprocal of a negative exponent flips it to positive, turning a thousandth into a thousand, a factor of a million away from the target.

questions.question: What is (3 × 10^4) × (2 × 10^5) expressed in correct scientific notation?
questions.explanation: Multiply the coefficients and add the exponents separately: (3 × 2) × 10^(4+5) = 6 × 10^9. The coefficient 6 is already in the range [1, 10), so no normalization is needed. Final answer: 6 × 10^9.
questions.trap: Students choose B (6 × 10^20) by multiplying the exponents (4 × 5 = 20) instead of adding them. When multiplying numbers in scientific notation, exponents are ADDED, not multiplied.

questions.question: What is (5 x 10^3)(4 x 10^6) expressed in correct scientific notation?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — split the problem in two: coefficients with coefficients, powers with powers.
Step 2 — coefficients: 5 x 4 = 20.
Step 3 — powers: 10^3 x 10^6 = 10^(3+6) = 10^9. So far: 20 x 10^9.
Step 4 — renormalise. Correct scientific notation requires the coefficient a to satisfy 1 <= a < 10, and 20 does not, so write 20 = 2 x 10^1 and absorb the extra power:
20 x 10^9 = 2 x 10^1 x 10^9 = 2 x 10^10.
Check: 5,000 x 4,000,000 = 20,000,000,000 = 2 x 10^10. Correct.
questions.trap: Choice D, 20 x 10^9, is the right number in the wrong form - the arithmetic is finished but the renormalising step is skipped, and GRE options are always in proper standard form. Choice B is the mirror error: the coefficient is renormalised to 2 but the freed power of 10 is thrown away instead of being added to the exponent. Choice E multiplies the exponents (3 x 6 = 18) instead of adding them, and choice A adds the coefficients (5 + 4 = 9).

questions.question: If 4.8 x 10^n = 480,000, what is the value of n? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — isolate the power: 10^n = 480,000/4.8 = 100,000.
Step 2 — 100,000 = 10^5, so n = 5.
Alternative route, by moving the point: to turn 4.8 into 480,000 the decimal point travels 4.8 -> 48 -> 480 -> 4,800 -> 48,000 -> 480,000, which is five places to the left, so n = 5.
Check: 4.8 x 100,000 = 480,000. Correct.
Answer: 5.
questions.trap: Answering 4 by counting the zeros in 480,000. Zeros are not the exponent unless the coefficient is a single digit followed only by zeros. Here the leading digit 4 sits in the hundred-thousands place, which is 10^5, so five places of movement are needed even though only four zeros are visible.

questions.question:
Column A: (2 x 10^3)^2
Column B: 4 x 10^6
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — the outer power hits BOTH factors: (2 x 10^3)^2 = 2^2 x (10^3)^2.
Step 2 — square the coefficient: 2^2 = 4.
Step 3 — square the power: (10^3)^2 = 10^(3x2) = 10^6. Note that a power of a power MULTIPLIES the exponents.
Step 4 — Column A = 4 x 10^6, which is exactly Column B.
Check in full: 2,000^2 = 4,000,000 = 4 x 10^6. Correct.
The two quantities are equal.
questions.trap: Squaring only the power of 10 and leaving the coefficient alone gives 2 x 10^6 = 2,000,000, which makes Column B look greater. The other slip is adding the exponents, (10^3)^2 = 10^5, which also points to Column B. Everything inside the bracket gets squared, and a power raised to a power multiplies.

questions.question: Which of the following is greater than 5 × 10^7?
questions.trap: Students choose E (A only) by dismissing option B — they think a coefficient only slightly larger (5.1 vs 5.0) with the SAME exponent cannot be greater. But 5.1 × 10^7 = 51,000,000 is definitively greater than 50,000,000.

questions.question:
Column A: 10^(-3)
Column B: (0.1)^3
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation:
Column A: 10^(-3) = 1/10^3 = 1/1000 = 0.001.
Column B: rewrite the base as a power of 10 first. 0.1 = 10^(-1), so (0.1)^3 = (10^(-1))^3 = 10^(-1 x 3) = 10^(-3).
Both columns equal 0.001, so the two quantities are equal.
Check by direct multiplication: 0.1 x 0.1 x 0.1 = 0.01 x 0.1 = 0.001. Correct.
questions.trap: Computing (0.1)^3 as 0.1 x 3 = 0.3, which makes Column B look much greater. Cubing a number between 0 and 1 makes it SMALLER, not larger. The reliable move is to convert every decimal to a power of 10 before doing anything else - once 0.1 becomes 10^(-1), the comparison is a one-line exponent calculation.

questions.question: A bacteria culture contains approximately 3.2 × 10^8 bacteria. If the count doubles, how many bacteria are there, expressed in correct scientific notation?
questions.explanation: Doubling 3.2 × 10^8 means multiplying by 2: 2 × (3.2 × 10^8) = (2 × 3.2) × 10^8 = 6.4 × 10^8. The coefficient 6.4 is between 1 and 10, so no normalization needed.
questions.trap: Students choose A (3.2 × 10^16) by squaring the entire expression — they confuse 'doubling' (multiplying by 2) with 'squaring' (raising to the power of 2). Doubling only multiplies the coefficient by 2.

questions.question: What is (6 × 10^7) ÷ (3 × 10^4)? Give your answer in standard form.
questions.explanation: Divide the coefficients and subtract the exponents: (6 ÷ 3) × 10^(7-4) = 2 × 10^3 = 2 × 1000 = 2000.
questions.trap: Students subtract the exponents in the wrong order, computing 10^(4-7) = 10^(-3) = 0.002 instead of 10^(7-4) = 10^3 = 1000. The divisor's exponent is subtracted FROM the dividend's exponent.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers have a NEGATIVE exponent when written in scientific notation? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation:
The test is one line: a number has a negative exponent exactly when it is strictly between 0 and 1.
A - 0.0083 = 8.3 x 10^(-3). Negative. TRUE.
B - 8,300 = 8.3 x 10^3. Positive. FALSE.
C - 0.83 = 8.3 x 10^(-1). It is less than 1, so the exponent is negative even though the number looks 'close to 1'. TRUE.
D - 1 = 1 x 10^0. Zero is not negative, so this fails the test. FALSE.
E - 0.00083 = 8.3 x 10^(-4). Negative. TRUE.
Answer: A, C, E.
questions.trap: Missing C because 0.83 does not look small. Any number below 1 - even 0.99 - has a negative exponent. D is the boundary case: 1 = 1 x 10^0, and 10^0 = 1, not 0, so its exponent is zero, which is neither positive nor negative.

questions.question:
Column A: 10^12 ÷ 10^8
Column B: 10^3 × 10^2
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.trap: A common error is computing Column A as 10^(12×8) instead of 10^(12−8). Division of powers → subtract exponents.

questions.question: Let X = 0.72 x 10^(-3), Y = 9.1 x 10^(-4), and Z = 830 x 10^(-6). Which of the following orders these three numbers from least to greatest?
questions.explanation:
None of these is in standard form except Y, so renormalise everything to a common footing first.
Step 1 — X = 0.72 x 10^(-3). Move the point one place right and drop the exponent by 1: X = 7.2 x 10^(-4) = 0.00072.
Step 2 — Y = 9.1 x 10^(-4) = 0.00091.
Step 3 — Z = 830 x 10^(-6). Move the point two places left and raise the exponent by 2: Z = 8.3 x 10^(-4) = 0.00083.
Step 4 — all three now share the exponent -4, so compare coefficients: 7.2 < 8.3 < 9.1.
Therefore X < Z < Y.
Check: 0.00072 < 0.00083 < 0.00091. Correct.
questions.trap: Choice D comes from comparing the exponents exactly as printed, -6 < -4 < -3, which puts Z smallest and X largest - the reverse of the truth for X. That shortcut is only legal once every coefficient is in [1, 10). Choice A comes from ranking by coefficient alone (0.72 < 9.1 < 830), choice C from renormalising X and Y but leaving Z at 10^(-6) and assuming it must therefore be the smallest, and choice E is the correct ranking written greatest-to-least when least-to-greatest was asked.

questions.question: The distance from Earth to the Sun is approximately 1.5 x 10^8 km, and the distance from Earth to the Moon is approximately 3.8 x 10^5 km. Approximately how many times as far from Earth is the Sun as the Moon? Round to the nearest whole number and enter your answer as a number.
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — 'how many times as far' means divide, so form (1.5 x 10^8)/(3.8 x 10^5).
Step 2 — split it: coefficients divide, exponents subtract.
coefficients: 1.5/3.8 = 0.3947...
exponents: 10^(8-5) = 10^3
Step 3 — 0.3947 x 10^3 = 394.7...
Step 4 — round: 395.
Order-of-magnitude sanity check: 1.5/3.8 is a bit under 0.4, and 0.4 x 1,000 = 400, so the answer must be a three-digit number just under 400. Correct.
Answer: 395.
questions.trap: Subtracting the exponents in the wrong order, 10^(5-8) = 10^(-3), which gives 0.395 - a Sun closer than the Moon, which the sanity check kills instantly. The dividend's exponent comes first. The other slip is reading 0.3947 x 10^3 as 3.947 or as 39.47 by mis-shifting the point.

questions.question:
Column A: (10^3)^4
Column B: (10^4)^3
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.trap: Students intuitively guess Column B is larger because the exponent 4 is in the 'outer' position for Column B. In fact, both equal 10^12 because multiplication is commutative: 3×4 = 4×3.

questions.question: A computer can perform 2.5 × 10^9 calculations per second. How many calculations can it perform in 4 × 10^2 seconds?
questions.trap: 2.5 × 4 = 10 = 10^1. Don't forget to combine this extra factor of 10 with 10^11 to get 10^12, not 10^11.

questions.question: Which of the following expressions are equal to 10^6? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation:
A - a power of a power multiplies exponents: (10^2)^3 = 10^(2x3) = 10^6. TRUE.
B - division subtracts exponents: 10^12/10^2 = 10^(12-2) = 10^10, not 10^6. FALSE.
C - multiplication adds exponents, and a negative exponent is just a negative addend: 10^8 x 10^(-2) = 10^(8 + (-2)) = 10^6. TRUE.
D - addition does not touch exponents at all: 10^3 + 10^3 = 2 x 10^3 = 2,000. FALSE.
E - multiply the exponents, keeping both signs: (10^(-2))^(-3) = 10^((-2)x(-3)) = 10^6. TRUE.
Answer: A, C, E.
questions.trap: B is the sharpest bait: 12/2 = 6, so dividing the exponents lands on the target by an illegal route - division of same-base powers subtracts, giving 10^10. D catches the belief that adding two equal powers combines their exponents; it only doubles the coefficient, leaving 2,000. E is dropped by students who see two minus signs and expect a small number, when two negatives multiply to a positive exponent.

questions.question:
x is a positive integer.
Column A: 10^(2x)
Column B: (10^x)^2
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: Column B: (10^x)^2 = 10^(x×2) = 10^(2x). This is identical to Column A. For any positive integer x, both columns equal 10^(2x). They are always equal.
questions.trap: Students try specific values and think the answer depends on x, choosing D. But (10^x)^2 = 10^(2x) is an algebraic identity — it holds for all values of x, making the relationship always equal.

questions.question: Given that 2^10 is approximately 10^3, approximately how many digits does 2^40 have?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — rewrite 2^40 so the given approximation can be used: 2^40 = (2^10)^4.
Step 2 — substitute: (2^10)^4 is approximately (10^3)^4 = 10^(3x4) = 10^12.
Step 3 — convert an order of magnitude into a digit count. 10^12 is a 1 followed by 12 zeros, which is 13 characters, so any number of size about 10^12 has 13 digits.
The general rule: a positive integer N with 10^(k) <= N < 10^(k+1) has k + 1 digits.
Check against the true value: 2^40 = 1,099,511,627,776, which indeed has 13 digits. Correct.
questions.trap: Choice B, 12, reads the exponent itself as the digit count; the count is always exponent + 1 for a number of size 10^k. Choice D applies that same 'exponent + 1' rule to the wrong exponent, the 40 in 2^40. Choice E comes from attaching the outer power to the approximation as (10^3)^40 = 10^120 and then adding 1, and choice A reads the outer exponent 4 as the answer.

questions.question: If 10^x = 5 x 10^7 and 10^y = 2 x 10^3, what is the value of x + y? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.explanation:
The insight: never solve for x and y separately. An exponent sum becomes a product.
Step 1 — 10^(x+y) = 10^x x 10^y.
Step 2 — substitute the two given values:
10^(x+y) = (5 x 10^7)(2 x 10^3)
Step 3 — coefficients multiply, exponents add: (5 x 2) x 10^(7+3) = 10 x 10^10.
Step 4 — renormalise: 10 x 10^10 = 10^1 x 10^10 = 10^11.
Step 5 — since 10^(x+y) = 10^11 and the bases match, x + y = 11 exactly.
Answer: 11.
questions.trap: The setup is engineered so the coefficients multiply to exactly 10; a student who writes 10 x 10^10 and reads off the exponent answers 10. That extra factor of 10 must be folded in, pushing the exponent to 11. The other route - x = log(5) + 7 = 7.699 and y = log(2) + 3 = 3.301 - is slow and invites rounding error, and no logarithm is needed here.

questions.question:
Column A: (3 x 10^(-4)) - (2 x 10^(-5))
Column B: 2.8 x 10^(-4)
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation:
Adding or subtracting in scientific notation requires MATCHING exponents first - only then may the coefficients be combined.
Step 1 — rewrite the second term with exponent -4. Moving from 10^(-5) up to 10^(-4) raises the exponent by 1, so the coefficient must shrink by a factor of 10:
2 x 10^(-5) = 0.2 x 10^(-4)
Step 2 — subtract the coefficients: (3 - 0.2) x 10^(-4) = 2.8 x 10^(-4).
Step 3 — that is exactly Column B, so the two quantities are equal.
Check in decimals: 0.0003 - 0.00002 = 0.00028 = 2.8 x 10^(-4). Correct.
questions.trap: Subtracting the coefficients as they stand, 3 - 2 = 1, and reporting 1 x 10^(-4) or 1 x 10^(-5) - both make Column B look greater. The exponents are one apart, so 2 x 10^(-5) is only a tenth of a unit of 10^(-4), not two units. The mirror error is shifting the point the wrong way, turning 2 x 10^(-5) into 20 x 10^(-4), which would make Column A negative.

questions.question: The mass of a proton is approximately 1.67 x 10^(-27) kg and the mass of an electron is approximately 9.11 x 10^(-31) kg. Approximately how many times as heavy as an electron is a proton?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — 'how many times as heavy' means proton divided by electron:
(1.67 x 10^(-27)) / (9.11 x 10^(-31))
Step 2 — exponents subtract, and subtracting a negative adds: -27 - (-31) = -27 + 31 = 4. So the power is 10^4.
Step 3 — coefficients divide: 1.67/9.11 = 0.183...
Step 4 — assemble and renormalise: 0.183 x 10^4 = 1.83 x 10^3, about 1,830.
Order-of-magnitude check: 1.67/9.11 is roughly 1/5.5, about 0.18, and 0.18 x 10,000 is about 1,800. Correct.
questions.trap: Choice A, 1.83 x 10^(-58), comes from -27 - 31 instead of -27 - (-31); subtracting a negative exponent adds. Choice D keeps the exponent at 4 after renormalising the coefficient from 0.183 to 1.83 - moving the point one place right must drop the exponent by 1. Choice E, 1.83 x 10^5, applies that same rule backwards and RAISES the exponent by 1. Choice B, 5.5 x 10^(-4), divides electron by proton, inverting the ratio.

questions.question: The quotient (2.4 x 10^8) / (8 x 10^(-4)) is written in scientific notation as a x 10^n, where 1 <= a < 10. What is the value of n? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — exponents subtract: 8 - (-4) = 8 + 4 = 12.
Step 2 — coefficients divide: 2.4/8 = 0.3.
Step 3 — the raw result is 0.3 x 10^12. The coefficient 0.3 is below 1, so this is not yet standard form.
Step 4 — renormalise. Move the point one place right (0.3 becomes 3) and drop the exponent by 1:
0.3 x 10^12 = 3 x 10^11
So a = 3 and n = 11.
Check: 3 x 10^11 x 8 x 10^(-4) = 24 x 10^7 = 2.4 x 10^8. Correct.
Answer: 11.
questions.trap: Answering 12 by reading the exponent off the raw result 0.3 x 10^12 without renormalising - a coefficient below 1 always costs the exponent one unit. Answering 4 comes from computing 8 - 4 instead of 8 - (-4); answering 3 from doing both errors at once.

questions.question: For which of the following values of n is (2 x 10^n)(5 x 10^(-4)) < 10^(-6)? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — simplify the left side once, in general. Coefficients: 2 x 5 = 10. Exponents: n + (-4) = n - 4.
(2 x 10^n)(5 x 10^(-4)) = 10 x 10^(n-4)
Step 2 — renormalise: the coefficient 10 is itself 10^1, so the product is 10^(n-4+1) = 10^(n-3).
Step 3 — the condition becomes 10^(n-3) < 10^(-6). Since 10^k grows with k, this is n - 3 < -6, i.e. n < -3.
Step 4 — test each option against n < -3:
A - n = -6 < -3. TRUE (value 10^(-9)).
B - n = -5 < -3. TRUE (value 10^(-8)).
C - n = -4 < -3. TRUE (value 10^(-7)).
D - n = -3 gives exactly 10^(-6), which is not LESS than 10^(-6). FALSE.
E - n = -2 gives 10^(-5), which is larger than 10^(-6). FALSE.
Answer: A, B, C.
questions.trap: The coefficients multiply to exactly 10, and a student who leaves the product as 10 x 10^(n-4) reads the exponent as n - 4 and solves n - 4 < -6, i.e. n < -2 - which wrongly admits D and E. D is the second trap on its own: at n = -3 the two sides are equal, and the inequality is strict, so equality does not qualify.

questions.question:
n is a positive integer.
Column A: 9 x 10^n + 10^n
Column B: 10^(n+1)
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — Column A is a sum of like terms. Factor out 10^n:
9 x 10^n + 10^n = (9 + 1) x 10^n = 10 x 10^n
Step 2 — renormalise the coefficient 10, which is 10^1:
10 x 10^n = 10^1 x 10^n = 10^(n+1)
Step 3 — that is exactly Column B, and no step used the value of n, so the two quantities are equal for every positive integer n.
Check with n = 3: Column A = 9,000 + 1,000 = 10,000; Column B = 10^4 = 10,000. Correct.
questions.trap: Assuming Column A must be smaller because 9 + 1 is only 10 while Column B is a whole extra power of ten - it is exactly the same thing, since ten copies of 10^n IS 10^(n+1). The opposite error is treating the sum as an exponent operation, 10^n + 10^n = 10^(2n), which would make Column A explode and point to A. Addition of like powers changes only the coefficient. Because the identity holds for every n, D is also wrong.

questions.question: In 2020 Country A had a GDP of 2.1 x 10^13 dollars and Country B had a GDP of 1.4 x 10^12 dollars. Country A's GDP was approximately what percent GREATER than Country B's GDP?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — get the ratio first; in scientific notation this is one line.
A/B = (2.1 x 10^13)/(1.4 x 10^12) = (2.1/1.4) x 10^(13-12) = 1.5 x 10^1 = 15
So A is 15 times B.
Step 2 — 'percent greater' measures the EXCESS over B, divided by B:
(A - B)/B x 100 = (15B - B)/B x 100 = 14 x 100 = 1,400%
Check: 1,400% of 1.4 x 10^12 is 14 x 1.4 x 10^12 = 1.96 x 10^13, and adding B back gives 1.96 x 10^13 + 0.14 x 10^13 = 2.1 x 10^13. Correct.
Answer: 1,400%.
questions.trap: Choice E, 1,500%, is the main bait: it uses the ratio 15 directly instead of the excess 14. 'A is 15 times B' and 'A is 1,400% greater than B' describe the same fact - the 1 in the 15 is B itself and must be stripped out. Choice C mistakes the ratio 15 for 150%, choice A mistakes it for 15%, and choice B divides the difference by A instead of B: 1.96 x 10^13 / 2.1 x 10^13 = 93%.

questions.question: If 10^a = 64 and 10^b = 0.25, what is the value of 10^(a + 2b)? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.explanation:
The insight: translate the exponent arithmetic into ordinary arithmetic on the given values. No logarithms are needed.
Step 1 — a sum in the exponent becomes a product: 10^(a + 2b) = 10^a x 10^(2b).
Step 2 — a multiple in the exponent becomes a power: 10^(2b) = (10^b)^2 = (0.25)^2 = 0.0625.
Step 3 — multiply the two known pieces: 10^(a+2b) = 64 x 0.0625.
Step 4 — 0.0625 = 1/16, so 64 x 1/16 = 4.
Answer: 4.
questions.trap: Doubling the value instead of squaring it - reading 10^(2b) as 2 x 10^b = 0.5, which gives 64 x 0.5 = 32. The 2 multiplies the EXPONENT, so it becomes a square on the value. The slow alternative, a = log(64) = 1.806 and b = log(0.25) = -0.602, then 10^(1.806 - 1.204) = 10^0.602, is both tedious and vulnerable to rounding.

questions.question:
Column A: The number of zeros between the decimal point and the first nonzero digit when (2 x 10^(-4))(5 x 10^(-3)) is written as a decimal
Column B: 6
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — multiply. Coefficients: 2 x 5 = 10. Exponents: -4 + (-3) = -7. Raw result: 10 x 10^(-7).
Step 2 — renormalise. The coefficient 10 is 10^1, so 10 x 10^(-7) = 10^(1-7) = 10^(-6) = 1 x 10^(-6).
Step 3 — turn the exponent into a zero count. In a x 10^(-k) with 1 <= a < 10, the first nonzero digit sits in the k-th decimal place, so exactly k - 1 zeros stand between the decimal point and it.
Here k = 6, so there are 5 zeros.
Check by writing it out: 10^(-6) = 0.000001 - five zeros, then the 1. Correct.
Column A = 5, Column B = 6, so Column B is greater.
questions.trap: Two errors both land on 6 and point at C. First, stopping at 10 x 10^(-7) and using k = 7, which gives 7 - 1 = 6. Second, renormalising correctly to 10^(-6) but then reporting the exponent 6 as the zero count. The first significant digit occupies one of those decimal places, so the zero count is always one less than the size of the exponent.

questions.question: If N = (10^24 - 1)/(10^8 - 1), which of the following is equal to N?
questions.explanation:
The insight: substitute a single letter for the repeated power so the structure becomes visible.
Step 1 — let x = 10^8. Then 10^24 = (10^8)^3 = x^3, and
N = (x^3 - 1)/(x - 1)
Step 2 — factor the numerator with the difference-of-cubes identity:
x^3 - 1 = (x - 1)(x^2 + x + 1)
Step 3 — cancel the (x - 1):
N = x^2 + x + 1
Step 4 — substitute back: x^2 = (10^8)^2 = 10^16, so
N = 10^16 + 10^8 + 1
Check: 10^16 + 10^8 + 1 = 10,000,000,100,000,001, and multiplying by 10^8 - 1 = 99,999,999 returns 10^24 - 1. Correct.
questions.trap: Choice B is the reflex answer, 10^(24-8) = 10^16, which would be right only if the two '-1's were not there; they are what forces a factorisation rather than a quotient of powers. Choice A divides the exponents, 24/8 = 3. Choice D applies the SUM-of-cubes pattern x^3 + 1 = (x + 1)(x^2 - x + 1) to a difference, flipping the sign of the middle term.

questions.question: The number 10^100 is called a googol. When 1/(4 x 10^100) is written as a decimal, how many zeros lie between the decimal point and the first nonzero digit? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — split the reciprocal into coefficient and power:
1/(4 x 10^100) = (1/4) x 10^(-100) = 0.25 x 10^(-100)
Step 2 — renormalise, since 0.25 is below 1. Move the point one place right and drop the exponent by 1:
0.25 x 10^(-100) = 2.5 x 10^(-101)
Step 3 — convert the exponent into a position. In a x 10^(-k) with 1 <= a < 10, the first nonzero digit occupies the k-th decimal place. Here k = 101, so the digit 2 sits in the 101st place.
Step 4 — the digit itself uses up one of those 101 places, so the zeros before it number 101 - 1 = 100.
Check the rule on a small case: 2.5 x 10^(-3) = 0.0025 - the 2 is in the 3rd decimal place and there are 2 zeros in front of it. Correct.
Answer: 100.
questions.trap: Answering 101 by reporting the exponent itself; the leading significant digit occupies one decimal place, so the zero count is always one less than the exponent's size. Answering 99 is the other end of the same confusion: it comes from stopping at 0.25 x 10^(-100), reading the exponent as 100 and subtracting 1, which ignores the extra place the renormalisation just cost.

questions.question:
p and q are nonnegative integers with p > q.
Column A: 10^p - 10^q
Column B: 10^(p - q)
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation:
The stem allows q = 0, and that boundary case reverses the comparison. Test both regions.
Case 1 - q = 0. Then Column A = 10^p - 1 and Column B = 10^(p-0) = 10^p. Subtracting 1 from 10^p leaves something strictly smaller than 10^p, so Column B is greater.
Example: p = 3, q = 0 gives A = 1,000 - 1 = 999 and B = 1,000. Column B wins.
Case 2 - q >= 1. Factor Column A: 10^p - 10^q = 10^q(10^(p-q) - 1). Write m = p - q >= 1. Then
Column A = 10^q x (10^m - 1) >= 10 x (10^m - 1) = 10^(m+1) - 10
and since m >= 1, 10^(m+1) - 10 >= 10^m x 10 - 10 > 10^m = Column B.
Example: p = 3, q = 1 gives A = 1,000 - 10 = 990 and B = 10^2 = 100. Column A wins.
Both outcomes occur, so the relationship cannot be determined.
questions.trap: Testing only q = 1, 2, 3 - where Column A always wins by a wide margin - and confidently choosing A. The single case q = 0 flips it, because then Column B stops being a small leftover and becomes the full 10^p, one unit above Column A. On any QC with 'nonnegative', deliberately test the value 0 before committing.

questions.question: Let S = 10^1 + 10^2 + 10^3 + ... + 10^9. Which of the following are true? Select all that apply.
options: D. The sum of the digits of S equals 9
questions.explanation:
Write S out first - the powers of 10 stack into a single pattern of 1s.
S = 10 + 100 + 1,000 + ... + 1,000,000,000 = 1,111,111,110 (nine 1s followed by one 0).
A - 10^10 = 10,000,000,000, and S = 1,111,111,110 is well below it. TRUE.
B - S = 1.11111111 x 10^9, which is LESS than 1.2 x 10^9. FALSE.
C - S has nine 1s and a final 0, so 10 digits. Equivalently 10^9 <= S < 10^10, and any such integer has 10 digits. TRUE.
D - the digits are nine 1s and one 0, summing to 9. TRUE.
E - the correct closed form is S = 10(10^9 - 1)/9 = (10^10 - 10)/9. The option has 10^9 where 10^10 belongs: (10^9 - 10)/9 = 999,999,990/9 = 111,111,110, which is S with one term missing. FALSE.
Answer: A, C, D.
questions.trap: B is the estimation bait: nine terms each 'about a billion' feels like several billion, but the series is dominated by its single largest term - everything below 10^9 adds only about 11% more, so S sits just past 1.11 x 10^9, not past 1.2 x 10^9. E is the off-by-one in the geometric-sum formula: the top exponent in the closed form is 10, not 9, because the sum ends at 10^9 rather than 10^8.

questions.question: What is 35% of 200?
questions.trap: Students often confuse 35% of 200 with 200% of 35 — both give 70 here, but the method matters for harder variants.

questions.question: A shirt is priced at $80. During a sale it is marked 25% off. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — turn the discount into a multiplier. Paying after 25% off means paying 100% - 25% = 75% of the price, so the multiplier is 0.75.
Step 2 — multiply. 0.75 x 80 = 60.
Check: the discount is 0.25 x 80 = $20, and 80 - 20 = $60. Correct.
Sale price = $60.
questions.trap: Choosing $20, which is the discount rather than the price paid. The second trap is reading '25% off' as '$25 off', which gives $55.

questions.question: 45 is what percent of 150? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — classify. This is 'find the percent': part is given, whole is given.
Step 2 — the base is the number after 'of', so 150 goes on the bottom.
45/150 = 3/10 = 0.3.
Step 3 — convert to percent: 0.3 x 100 = 30.
Answer: 30.
questions.trap: Dividing the other way, 150/45 = 3.33, and answering 333. Whatever follows the word 'of' is always the denominator.

questions.question: A class has 40 students. If 60% are girls, how many boys are in the class?
questions.explanation: 60% are girls → 40% are boys. 40% of 40 = 0.40 × 40 = 16 boys.
questions.trap: Finding girls (24) instead of boys is the most common error here.

questions.question:
Column A: 20% of 80
Column B: 80% of 20
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: Column A: 20% of 80 = 0.20 × 80 = 16. Column B: 80% of 20 = 0.80 × 20 = 16. They are equal. This illustrates the commutative property of percentages: x% of y = y% of x.
questions.trap: Students assume the larger percentage (80%) paired with the smaller number yields a different result. The symmetry here is a key GRE concept.

questions.question: If 30% of a number is 48, what is the number?
questions.trap: Students multiply 48 × 0.30 = 14.4 instead of dividing, or guess 140 by adding 48 + 30×3.

questions.question: A store sells 120 items. If 15 items are returned, what percentage of items were returned? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.trap: Students may compute 120/15 = 8 and answer 8%, which is the inverse ratio.

questions.question:
A price increases from $50 to $60.
Column A: The percent increase
Column B: 20%
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation:
Percent change = (New - Old)/Old x 100.
Step 1 — the change: 60 - 50 = 10.
Step 2 — the base is the ORIGINAL value, 50.
Step 3 — 10/50 x 100 = 0.2 x 100 = 20%.
Column A = 20% = Column B, so the two quantities are equal.
questions.trap: Dividing the $10 change by the new price: 10/60 = 16.7%, which makes Column B look greater. Percent change divides by the value you started from, never the value you ended at.

questions.question: What is 150% of 60?
questions.explanation: 150% of 60 = 1.50 × 60 = 90. Percentages greater than 100% are common GRE traps — 150% means one-and-a-half times the number.
questions.trap: Students assume percentages must be less than 100 and choose 40 (thinking 150% means you subtract 150% of something).

questions.question: In a survey, 48 out of 64 respondents preferred option A. What percent preferred option A?
questions.trap: The fraction 48/64 simplifies to 3/4, which equals 75%. Students who don't simplify may miscalculate.

questions.question: After a 20% discount, a product sells for $240. What was the price before the discount, in dollars? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — build the multiplier. A 20% discount means the buyer pays 80%, so 0.80.
Step 2 — write the equation forwards: 0.80 x P = 240.
Step 3 — reverse it by dividing: P = 240/0.80 = 300.
Check: 20% of 300 = 60, and 300 - 60 = 240. Correct.
Answer: 300.
questions.trap: Adding 20% back to the sale price: 240 x 1.20 = 288. The 20% was taken off $300, not off $240, so you must divide by the multiplier rather than add the percent back on.

questions.question:
Column A: 10% of 10% of 1000
Column B: 1% of 1000
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: Column A: 10% of 1000 = 100; 10% of 100 = 10. Column B: 1% of 1000 = 10. Equal.
questions.trap: Students add percentages: 10% + 10% = 20%, thinking Column A = 20% of 1000 = 200.

questions.question: A school has 500 students. 40% are in Grade 9, and 25% of Grade 9 students play football. How many Grade 9 students play football?
questions.explanation: Grade 9 students: 40% of 500 = 200. Football players: 25% of 200 = 50.
questions.trap: Students compute 25% of 500 = 125 directly, skipping the intermediate step.

questions.question: A number is increased by 10%, and the result is then decreased by 10%. What is the net percent change?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — pick 100 as the starting value (legal, since the question is all percents).
Step 2 — up 10%: 100 x 1.10 = 110.
Step 3 — down 10%, applied to 110: 110 x 0.90 = 99.
Step 4 — net change = (99 - 100)/100 x 100 = -1%.
The one-line version: 1.10 x 0.90 = 0.99, a 1% decrease.
questions.trap: Answering 0% because +10% and -10% look like they cancel. They cannot: the rise is 10% of 100, but the fall is 10% of the larger number 110, so more comes off than went on. Up x% then down x% always loses exactly x^2/100 percent - here 100/100 = 1%.

questions.question: If a price increases by 25% and then decreases by 20%, what is the overall percent change? Enter your answer as a number (negative if a decrease).
questions.explanation: Start with 100. After +25%: 125. After -20% of 125: 125 × 0.80 = 100. Net change = 0%. This is a known GRE pattern: +25% then -20% always returns to the original.
questions.trap: Students add/subtract percentages: 25% - 20% = +5%. The actual result is 0%.

questions.question:
x is a positive number.
Column A: 50% of 2x
Column B: x
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: 50% of 2x = 0.50 × 2x = x. Column A = Column B always for any positive x.
questions.trap: Without simplifying algebraically, students may try x = 10 and then doubt their answer.

questions.question: A population of 800 bacteria increases by 50% each hour. What is the population after 2 hours?
questions.trap: Students compute 50% increase twice as +100% total: 800 × 2 = 1600. That ignores compounding.

questions.question: In a bag of 60 marbles, 45 are red. What percentage are NOT red?
questions.explanation: Non-red marbles: 60 - 45 = 15. Percentage: (15/60) × 100 = 25%.
questions.trap: Students find 45/60 = 75% and stop, forgetting the question asks for NOT red.

questions.question: A salesperson earns a 6% commission on all sales. If she sold goods worth $4,500, what is her commission in dollars? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.trap: Students may compute 4500/6 = 750, confusing division with percentage.

questions.question: Which of the following are equal to 0.4%? Select all that apply.
questions.trap: The decimal placement is the entire challenge here. 0.4% is much smaller than it looks.

questions.question: A laptop's price is reduced from $1,200 to $900. By what percent was the price reduced?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — the change: 1200 - 900 = 300.
Step 2 — the base is the original price, 1200.
Step 3 — 300/1200 = 1/4 = 25%.
Answer: 25%.
questions.trap: Dividing by the new price: 300/900 = 33 1/3%, which is choice D. A second trap is 900/1200 = 75%, which is the fraction of the price that REMAINS, not the reduction.

questions.question: In 2022, a company had revenue of $5 million. In 2023, revenue grew by 12%. In 2024, it grew by another 15%. What was the 2024 revenue in millions of dollars? Enter your answer rounded to two decimal places.
questions.trap: Students add 12% + 15% = 27% and compute 5 × 1.27 = 6.35 million. Compounding matters.

questions.question:
A jacket costs $150. Store A offers a 30% discount followed by an additional 10% off the discounted price. Store B offers a flat 40% discount.
Column A: Final price at Store A
Column B: Final price at Store B
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation:
Store A - build one chain: 150 x 0.70 x 0.90.
0.70 x 0.90 = 0.63, so 150 x 0.63 = $94.50.
Store B: 150 x 0.60 = $90.00.
$94.50 > $90.00, so Column A is greater.
questions.trap: Reading 30% then 10% as a combined 40% and choosing C. Successive discounts never add: 0.70 x 0.90 = 0.63, an effective 37% off, because the 10% is taken from an already reduced price. Two successive discounts are always weaker than their sum.

questions.question: A solution is 40% alcohol by volume. If 50 ml of water is added to 200 ml of this solution, what is the new percentage of alcohol?
questions.explanation: Alcohol in original solution: 40% of 200 = 80 ml. New total volume: 200 + 50 = 250 ml. New alcohol %: (80/250) × 100 = 32%.
questions.trap: Students subtract 50 from 40% mentally without computing actual volumes, or forget to add to total volume.

questions.question: The price of an item increased from $P to $1.3P, where P > 0. Which of the following statements must be true? Select all that apply.
options: C. The new price is 130% of the original
D. The new price is greater than the original
E. The percent increase depends on the value of P
questions.explanation:
A - percent increase = (1.3P - P)/P x 100 = 0.3P/P x 100 = 30%. The P cancels, so this is true for every P. TRUE.
B - the increase is 0.3P dollars, not $0.30. That would only be right if P = $1. FALSE.
C - 1.3P = 130% of P by definition of the multiplier. TRUE.
D - since P > 0, 1.3P > P. TRUE.
E - the P cancelled in A, so the percent increase is 30% for every P. FALSE.
Answer: A, C, D.
questions.trap: Picking B by reading the 0.3 as a dollar amount instead of a coefficient, and picking E because P is unknown. When the unknown cancels out of the ratio, the percent is fixed even though the dollar change is not.

questions.question: After a 20% increase followed by a 20% decrease, a number becomes 576. What was the original number? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — build the whole chain first: 1.20 x 0.80 = 0.96.
Step 2 — 0.96 x N = 576.
Step 3 — reverse by dividing: N = 576/0.96 = 600.
Check: 600 -> 720 -> 720 x 0.80 = 576. Correct.
Answer: 600.
questions.trap: Assuming +20% and -20% cancel, so the original 'must' be 576. The chain is 0.96, a 4% net fall, which is exactly 20^2/100 percent.

questions.question:
Column A: The percent increase when a quantity goes from 80 to 100
Column B: The percent decrease when a quantity goes from 100 to 80
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation:
Column A: change = 20, base = 80 (where you started), so 20/80 x 100 = 25%.
Column B: change = 20, base = 100 (where you started), so 20/100 x 100 = 20%.
25% > 20%, so Column A is greater.
questions.trap: Both moves cover the same 20 units, so students pick C. The base flips: going up you divide by 80, coming down you divide by 100. A rise and the fall that undoes it are never the same percent.

questions.question: At a restaurant, a meal costs $48. A 15% tip is added, followed by an 8% tax on the total including the tip. What is the final amount paid?
questions.trap: Students compute tip and tax separately on the base price and add: 48 + 7.20 + 3.84 = $59.04. But tax is applied on price + tip.

questions.question: In an election, candidate A received 56% of 25,000 votes. Candidate B received the remaining votes. By how many votes did A win?
questions.trap: Students compute A's votes (14,000) and stop, or compute the difference as 56-44=12 but then forget to apply it to 25,000.

questions.question: A retailer buys goods for $360 and marks them up by 40%. He then gives a 10% discount on the marked price. What is his profit percentage on cost price? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.trap: Students subtract 10% from 40% to get 30% profit. Successive operations on different bases don't add/subtract linearly.

questions.question:
P and Q are positive integers where P > Q.
Column A: Q as a percent of P
Column B: P as a percent of Q
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: Column A = (Q/P) × 100. Column B = (P/Q) × 100. Since P > Q > 0, Q/P < 1 < P/Q. So Column A < Column B always.
questions.trap: Students may try specific numbers but overlook that the relationship is guaranteed by P > Q.

questions.question: A town's population increased by 20% in the first decade and decreased by 10% in the second decade. Which of the following are true? Select all that apply.
options: A. The net change over 20 years is +8%
B. The population at the end of year 20 is 1.08 times the original
C. If the original population was 10,000, the final population is 10,800
D. The percent increase in decade 1 is greater than the percent decrease in decade 2
E. The population could return to its original value if it decreased by exactly 20% in the third decade
questions.explanation: Net multiplier: 1.20 × 0.90 = 1.08 → +8% net change. A ✓, B ✓, C: 10,000 × 1.08 = 10,800 ✓, D: 20% > 10% ✓. E: To return to original from 10,800, need (10,800 - 10,000)/10,800 ≈ 7.4% decrease, not 20%. E is false.
questions.trap: E is the sneaky one — students may compute incorrectly or assume a 20% decrease reverses a 20% increase (it doesn't).

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells two items for $240 each. On one he makes a 20% profit; on the other he takes a 20% loss. Overall, what is his profit or loss percent?
questions.explanation:
Selling price is given, so work backwards to each cost.
Step 1 — profit item: SP = 1.20 x CP, so CP = 240/1.20 = $200.
Step 2 — loss item: SP = 0.80 x CP, so CP = 240/0.80 = $300.
Step 3 — totals: cost = 200 + 300 = $500; revenue = 2 x 240 = $480.
Step 4 — loss = $20 on a cost of $500 = 20/500 x 100 = 4% loss.
questions.trap: Assuming equal selling prices with equal +20%/-20% cancel out. They cannot: the loss item cost more ($300 vs $200), so the loss is taken on a bigger base. Whenever two items sell for the SAME price at +x% and -x%, the result is always a loss of x^2/100 percent - here 4%.

questions.question: In a company, 60% of employees are full-time, and 75% of full-time employees have health insurance. If 180 full-time employees have health insurance, how many total employees does the company have? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.explanation: Full-time with insurance = 75% of full-time = 180 → full-time = 180/0.75 = 240. Full-time = 60% of total → total = 240/0.60 = 400.
questions.trap: Students solve one step and stop at 240, or divide incorrectly.

questions.question: The price of oil increased by 25% in January and decreased by 16% in February. What is the net percent change over the two months?
questions.explanation: Net multiplier: 1.25 × 0.84 = 1.05. Net change = +5%.
questions.trap: Students subtract: 25% - 16% = +9% (answer C). Must multiply the multipliers, not subtract the percentages.

questions.question:
Column A: 40% of 3/5 of 200
Column B: 60% of 2/5 of 200
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.trap: Students compute one column and guess without completing the other, or make arithmetic errors on the fractions.

questions.question: A student scored 72 marks out of 90 in one test and 78 marks out of 120 in another test. In which test did the student perform better, and by what percentage?
questions.explanation: First test: 72/90 × 100 = 80%. Second test: 78/120 × 100 = 65%. The student performed better in the first test by 80% − 65% = 15 percentage points. Answer: First test by 15%.
questions.trap: Be careful: the question asks 'by what percentage,' meaning the difference in percentage scores = 15 percentage points, not a percent-of-percent calculation.

questions.question: A mixture of juice is 30% mango and 70% orange. If 20 liters of mango juice is added to 100 liters of this mixture, what percent of the new mixture is mango juice? Enter your answer rounded to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: Original mango: 30% of 100 = 30 liters. Add 20L mango. Total mango = 50L, total mixture = 120L. New % = (50/120) × 100 = 41.7%.
questions.trap: Students add 20% to 30% = 50% without accounting for the change in total volume.

questions.question: A store marks up items by 50% and then offers a discount of d%. For what values of d does the store still make a profit? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: For profit: selling price > cost. 1.5C(1 - d/100) > C → d < 33.33%. Only A(20%) and B(33%) satisfy this. C, D, E all result in a loss.
questions.trap: Students think a 50% markup means any discount up to 50% is fine. The break-even discount is 33.3%, not 50%.

questions.question:
A number N is increased by 50% to get M.
Column A: The percent decrease needed to go from M back to N
Column B: 33.33%
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: N × 1.5 = M. To go from M to N: decrease = (M-N)/M = (1.5N - N)/1.5N = 0.5N/1.5N = 1/3 = 33.33%. Column A = Column B.
questions.trap: Students think if you increase by 50%, you decrease by 50% to get back. The decrease needed is always less than the increase because the base changed.

questions.question: An investor puts $10,000 in a fund. The fund gains 30% in year 1, loses 30% in year 2. What is the value of the investment after year 2?
questions.trap: Students answer $10,000 (choice D), thinking +30% and -30% cancel. They don't — the 30% loss is applied to the larger amount.

questions.question: If x% of y equals y% of 80, what is x? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.explanation: (x/100) × y = (y/100) × 80. Dividing both sides by y/100 (assuming y ≠ 0): x = 80.
questions.trap: Students try to solve for both x and y or assume specific values, missing the elegant algebraic cancellation.

questions.question: In a town, 55% of residents own a car and 40% own a bike. If 15% own both, what percent own neither?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — union by inclusion-exclusion: car OR bike = 55 + 40 - 15 = 80%.
Step 2 — neither is the complement of the union: 100 - 80 = 20%.
Answer: 20%.
questions.trap: Adding 55 + 40 = 95 and answering 5%. That double-counts the 15% who own both, so the union is overstated and 'neither' comes out too small. Subtract the overlap once before taking the complement.

questions.question:
Column A: 0.5% of 2000
Column B: 5% of 200
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.trap: Decimal placement errors — students may compute 0.5% as 0.5 instead of 0.005, getting 1000 for Column A.

questions.question: A sum of money is divided among three people in the ratio 2:3:5. The person with the largest share receives what percent more than the person with the smallest share?
questions.explanation: Smallest share = 2 parts, largest = 5 parts. Percent more = (5-2)/2 × 100 = 3/2 × 100 = 150%.
questions.trap: Students find the ratio 5:2 and say 'largest is 250% of smallest' — which is true but not what's asked. The question asks how much MORE, which is 150%.

questions.question: A number is 20% more than another number. The larger number is what percent of the smaller number? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.explanation: If smaller = 100, larger = 120. Larger as % of smaller = (120/100) × 100 = 120%.
questions.trap: Students confuse 'percent more than' (20%) with 'percent of' (120%). These are different questions.

questions.question: Which of the following percent changes result in a final value greater than the starting value? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A: 1.50×0.60=0.90 (loss). B: 1.25×0.80=1.00 (no change). C: 1.10×0.90=0.99 (loss). D: 2.00×0.50=1.00 (no change). E: 1.20×0.85=1.02 (gain). Only E results in a value greater than the start.
questions.trap: B and D look like they should gain but exactly cancel. The trap is assuming symmetric percentages always give gains.

questions.question: A company's revenue increased by 15% in Q1, decreased by 10% in Q2, increased by 20% in Q3, and decreased by 5% in Q4. If the starting revenue was $1,000,000, what is the approximate ending revenue?
questions.trap: Adding/subtracting percentages: 15-10+20-5=20%, giving 1,200,000. Compounding gives a different result.

questions.question:
x > 0
Column A: x increased by 50% then decreased by 50%
Column B: x decreased by 50% then increased by 50%
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: Column A: x × 1.5 × 0.5 = 0.75x. Column B: x × 0.5 × 1.5 = 0.75x. Both equal 0.75x — multiplication is commutative, so order doesn't matter here.
questions.trap: Students think one order is 'worse' than the other. Both give the same result: 25% loss.

questions.question: In a class, the boys averaged 75% on a test and the girls averaged 80%. The class as a whole averaged 78%. What percent of the class are boys? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.explanation:
Method 1 - weighted average. Let b be the fraction of boys.
75b + 80(1 - b) = 78
75b + 80 - 80b = 78
-5b = -2, so b = 0.4 = 40%.
Method 2 - alligation (faster). Distance from boys' mean to the class mean = 78 - 75 = 3. Distance from the class mean to the girls' mean = 80 - 78 = 2. The group sizes are in the INVERSE ratio of these distances, so boys : girls = 2 : 3, and boys = 2/5 = 40%.
Answer: 40.
questions.trap: Answering 60. The class average of 78 sits closer to the girls' 80, which means girls are the LARGER group - so boys must be the smaller share. In alligation the bigger group is the one nearer the overall mean, which flips the ratio you first write down.

questions.question: A retailer sells an item at a 25% profit on cost. The cost price then rises by 20% while the selling price is held unchanged. What is the new profit or loss percent?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — pick CP = 100. Then SP = 1.25 x 100 = 125.
Step 2 — the new cost: 100 x 1.20 = 120. The selling price stays at 125.
Step 3 — profit = 125 - 120 = 5, and profit percent is always taken on COST.
5/120 x 100 = 500/120 = 4.166... = 4.17% profit.
questions.trap: Two errors compete here. First, assuming a 20% cost rise must wipe out the margin and produce a loss - it does not, because the original markup was large enough to absorb it. Second, dividing by the selling price: 5/125 = 4%, which is choice B. Profit percent always divides by cost, and here that means the NEW cost of 120.

questions.question:
N and p are positive. A number N is increased by p%, and the result is then decreased by p%.
Column A: The final number
Column B: N
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation:
Final = N x (1 + p/100) x (1 - p/100).
This is a difference of squares: (1 + p/100)(1 - p/100) = 1 - p^2/10000.
Since p > 0, the term p^2/10000 is strictly positive, so the multiplier is strictly less than 1.
With N > 0, the final number is always less than N, whatever p is. Column B is greater.
The loss is exactly p^2/100 percent - for p = 10 that is 1%, for p = 20 it is 4%, for p = 50 it is 25%.
questions.trap: Choosing C because the same p goes up and comes back down. The rise is p% of N, but the fall is p% of the LARGER number N(1 + p/100), so more is removed than was added. Note the answer does not depend on the size of p, so D is also wrong.

questions.question: The price of a commodity falls by 20%. By what percent must consumption increase so that total expenditure is unchanged? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.explanation:
Expenditure = price x consumption, so for expenditure to be unchanged the two multipliers must multiply to 1.
Step 1 — price multiplier = 0.80.
Step 2 — consumption multiplier = 1/0.80 = 1.25.
Step 3 — 1.25 means a 25% increase.
Check with numbers: price 100 x quantity 10 = 1000. New price 80, so quantity must be 1000/80 = 12.5, up from 10 - a 25% rise. Correct.
Answer: 25.
questions.trap: Answering 20 to mirror the 20% price fall. Test it: 0.80 x 1.20 = 0.96, so expenditure would still be 4% lower. A fall of 1/5 needs a rise of 1/4 - a drop of 1/(n+1) always needs a rise of 1/n.

questions.question: In a school, 60% of students passed Math, 50% passed Science, and 25% failed both subjects. What percent of students passed BOTH subjects?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — 'failed both' is the complement of 'passed at least one', so the union is 100 - 25 = 75%.
Step 2 — inclusion-exclusion: (passed Math) + (passed Science) - (passed both) = (passed at least one).
60 + 50 - both = 75
Step 3 — both = 110 - 75 = 35%.
Check the four regions: both 35, Math only 25, Science only 15, neither 25. They sum to 100. Correct.
Answer: 35%.
questions.trap: Treating the 25% who failed both AS the overlap and answering 25% (choice C). Those 25% sit OUTSIDE both circles; the overlap has to be computed. The other slip is stopping at 75% - that is the union, the answer to a different question.

questions.question: A store offers successive discounts of 20%, 10%, and 5% on an item. Which of the following are true? Select all that apply.
options: B. The effective discount is less than 35%
C. The final price is 68.4% of the original
D. The order in which the three discounts are applied does not affect the final price
E. A single discount of 35% would give a lower final price than these three discounts
questions.explanation:
Build the chain: 0.80 x 0.90 x 0.95.
0.80 x 0.90 = 0.72, and 0.72 x 0.95 = 0.684.
So the final price is 68.4% of the original and the effective discount is 100 - 68.4 = 31.6%.
A - 31.6% is not 35%. FALSE.
B - 31.6% < 35%. TRUE.
C - final price = 68.4% of the original. TRUE.
D - multiplication is commutative, so any order gives 0.684. TRUE.
E - a single 35% discount leaves 65% of the price, and 65% < 68.4%, so it is the cheaper deal. TRUE.
Answer: B, C, D, E.
questions.trap: A is the obvious bait - adding 20 + 10 + 5. The subtler one is E: because successive discounts are weaker than their sum, the single 35% discount actually beats the three, so a student who reasons 'successive discounts must be better for the customer' gets E backwards.

questions.question:
A population grows at 10% per year for 3 years.
Column A: The total percentage increase over 3 years
Column B: 30%
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: After 3 years: (1.10)³ = 1.331. Total increase = 33.1%. Column A (33.1%) > Column B (30%). Compound growth always exceeds simple addition of annual rates.
questions.trap: Students add 10+10+10 = 30% and choose C. Compounding means each year's growth applies to a larger base.

questions.question: After two successive percent increases, a number becomes 1.44 times its original value. If both increases were equal, what was each increase? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.trap: Students split 44% into 22% each. That gives 1.22² = 1.4884 ≠ 1.44. Must use the square root.

questions.question: A mixture contains milk and water in ratio 4:1. How much water must be added to 100 liters of this mixture to make the ratio 4:3?
questions.explanation: Original: 80L milk, 20L water. New ratio milk:water = 4:3. Milk stays at 80L. If ratio is 4:3, then water = (3/4) × 80 = 60L. Water to add = 60 - 20 = 40L.
questions.trap: Students try to adjust both milk and water instead of realizing milk quantity is fixed.

questions.question:
x and y are positive numbers where x > y.
Column A: x% of y
Column B: y% of x
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: x% of y = (x/100) × y = xy/100. y% of x = (y/100) × x = xy/100. Always equal, regardless of which is larger.
questions.trap: Students assume x% of y is larger because x > y. The symmetry of percentage multiplication makes them always equal.

questions.question: A price P increases by x% to become Q, where 0 < P < Q. Which of the following expressions correctly represent x? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation:
The definition: x = (change / original) x 100 = (Q - P)/P x 100.
A - that is the definition itself. TRUE.
B - Q/P - 1 = (Q - P)/P, so multiplying by 100 gives the same thing. TRUE.
C - (Q/P) x 100 - 100 = 100(Q/P - 1) = 100(Q - P)/P. Same expression rearranged. TRUE.
D - divides by Q, the NEW price. That is the percent decrease going from Q back down to P, a different (smaller) number. FALSE.
E - identical to A, just written with the 100 in front. TRUE.
Answer: A, B, C, E.
questions.trap: D is the classic wrong formula and it looks symmetric with A, so it gets picked. The percent rise from P to Q and the percent fall from Q back to P are never equal, because they use different denominators.

questions.question: A's income is 30% more than B's. B's income is 20% less than C's. A's income is what percent of C's income? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — pick C = 100, since C is the base at the end of the chain.
Step 2 — B is 20% less than C: B = 0.80 x 100 = 80.
Step 3 — A is 30% more than B: A = 1.30 x 80 = 104.
Step 4 — A as a percent of C: 104/100 x 100 = 104%.
One-line version: 1.30 x 0.80 = 1.04.
Answer: 104.
questions.trap: Netting the percents to 30 - 20 = 10 and answering 110. The 30% is measured on B while the 20% is measured on C - different bases, so they cannot be added. Chain the multipliers instead.

questions.question: In 2020 the ratio of A's salary to B's salary was 3:4. In 2021 A's salary rose by 25% and B's salary fell by 25%. What is the new ratio of A's salary to B's salary?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — write the salaries as 3k and 4k so the ratio is preserved.
Step 2 — apply each multiplier to its own term:
new A = 3k x 1.25 = 3.75k
new B = 4k x 0.75 = 3k
Step 3 — the ratio: 3.75k : 3k = 3.75 : 3 = 375 : 300 = 5 : 4.
Answer: 5:4.
questions.trap: Expecting the +25% and -25% to cancel and leave the ratio at 3:4 (choice A) - they act on different salaries, so nothing cancels except k. Choice E, 15:16, is the other live error: raising A to 3.75 but forgetting to shrink B, which leaves 3.75:4 = 15:16.

questions.question:
A product's price increases by 10% each year for 7 years.
Column A: The total percent increase over the 7 years
Column B: 70%
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation:
The price multiplier is 1.10^7.
Build it in pieces: 1.10^2 = 1.21, so 1.10^4 = 1.21^2 = 1.4641, and 1.10^3 = 1.331.
1.10^7 = 1.10^4 x 1.10^3 = 1.4641 x 1.331 = 1.9487.
That is a 94.87% increase, comfortably above 70%. Column A is greater.
You do not even need the exact value: 1.10^7 = 1.10^4 x 1.10^3 > 1.4 x 1.3 = 1.82, already a 82% rise.
questions.trap: Multiplying 10% x 7 = 70% and choosing C. That is simple-interest thinking. Once there is more than one period, each year's rise is computed on a larger amount, so compound growth always exceeds the simple sum.

questions.question: The population of a city was 2,000,000 in 2010. It grew at 5% per year until 2015, then declined at 2% per year until 2020. What is the approximate population in 2020? Enter your answer rounded to the nearest thousand.
questions.trap: Students compute growth and decline phases separately as simple interest, or miscalculate compound multipliers.

questions.question: A number N is decreased by 40% to get M. Which of the following must be true? Select all that apply.
options: C. N is 66.67% more than M
D. M is 40% less than N
questions.explanation: M = 0.6N ✓ (A). N = M/0.6 ✓ (E). N is what % more than M? (N-M)/M = (N-0.6N)/0.6N = 0.4N/0.6N = 2/3 ≈ 66.67% ✓ (C). M is 40% less than N ✓ (D). B: N = M + 0.4M = 1.4M → M = N/1.4 ≈ 0.714N. But M = 0.6N. So B is false — the 40% reduction was on N, not on M.
questions.trap: B is subtly wrong — 40% of N ≠ 40% of M. Students confuse which base the percentage applies to.

questions.question: A dishonest dealer claims to sell goods at cost price, but his 'kilogram' weight is actually 900 grams. What is his real profit percent?
questions.explanation:
Set the true cost at $1 per gram.
Step 1 — the customer is charged for 1000 g, so revenue = $1000.
Step 2 — the dealer actually hands over 900 g, so his cost = $900.
Step 3 — profit = 1000 - 900 = $100, taken on a cost of $900.
100/900 x 100 = 11.11%.
General rule for false weights: profit % = (true weight - false weight)/false weight x 100.
questions.trap: Dividing by 1000 to get 10% (choice B). The 1000 is what he charged for - that is revenue, not cost. Profit percent is always taken on what he gave up, the 900 g actually delivered. Choice A, 9.09%, is 100/1100, from adding the shortfall to the kilo instead of subtracting it; choice D, 12.5%, is 100/800, from mistaking the false weight for 800 g.

questions.question:
An item's price increased by 20% and then by another 20%.
Column A: Overall percent increase
Column B: 44%
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: 1.20 × 1.20 = 1.44 → 44% overall increase. Column A = Column B.
questions.trap: Students compute 20 + 20 = 40% (Column B > Column A). The actual compound result is exactly 44%.

questions.question: A, B, and C are three numbers. A is 25% of B, and B is 80% of C. What percent of C is A? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.explanation: A = 0.25B and B = 0.80C. Therefore A = 0.25 × 0.80C = 0.20C = 20% of C.
questions.trap: Students add the percentages: 25 + 80 = 105% or try to subtract. Must multiply the decimal multipliers.

questions.question: An employee's salary increases by 10% every year. After how many complete years will the salary first exceed 150% of the current salary?
questions.explanation:
We need the smallest whole n with 1.10^n > 1.50.
1.10^2 = 1.21
1.10^3 = 1.331
1.10^4 = 1.4641 - still below 1.50
1.10^5 = 1.61051 - above 1.50
So the salary first exceeds 150% of its current value after 5 complete years.
Answer: 5.
questions.trap: Reading '150% of the current salary' as 'a 150% increase', which means 2.5 times the salary and takes 10 years (1.10^10 = 2.594) - choice E. 150% OF a number is 1.5 times it; a 150% INCREASE makes it 2.5 times. A second error is stopping at year 4 because 1.4641 looks close enough to 1.5.

questions.question: In a class, 70% of students passed English and 60% passed Math. Which of the following could be the percent who passed both? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation:
The overlap of two sets is squeezed between two bounds.
Maximum: the overlap can never exceed the smaller set, so both <= min(70, 60) = 60%.
Minimum: 70 + 60 = 130, but only 100% of the class exists, so at least 130 - 100 = 30% must be counted twice. So both >= 30%.
The overlap therefore satisfies 30% <= both <= 60%.
A (25%) is below the minimum. B (30%) is exactly at the minimum, achievable when everyone passed at least one. C (40%) and D (55%) are inside the range. E (65%) exceeds the smaller set.
Answer: B, C, D.
questions.trap: Assuming the overlap could be anything from 0 to 60 and including A. When the two percents sum to more than 100 there is not enough room to keep the groups apart, so a forced overlap of (sum - 100) exists. E catches the opposite error - forgetting that the overlap cannot be bigger than the smaller group.

questions.question: A merchant mixes tea costing $40 per kg with tea costing $60 per kg and sells the mixture at $60 per kg, making a 25% profit on his average cost. In what ratio, by weight, did he mix the two varieties?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 — recover the cost from the selling price. A 25% profit means SP = 1.25 x cost, so cost = 60/1.25 = $48 per kg.
Step 2 — alligation on the average cost of 48:
distance from the $40 tea: 48 - 40 = 8
distance from the $60 tea: 60 - 48 = 12
Step 3 — the quantities are in the INVERSE ratio of these distances: cheap : dear = 12 : 8 = 3 : 2.
Check: (3 x 40 + 2 x 60)/5 = (120 + 120)/5 = 240/5 = $48. Correct.
Answer: 3:2.
questions.trap: Two traps stack. First, taking 25% OFF the selling price (60 x 0.75 = 45) instead of dividing by 1.25 - profit is measured on cost, so the cost is SP/1.25 = 48, not 45. Second, writing the ratio as 8:12 = 2:3 (choice B): in alligation the quantities are the inverse of the distances, so the tea whose price is CLOSER to the average is the one you need MORE of.

questions.question:
p, q, r are three positive numbers where p < q < r.
Column A: p% of q% of r
Column B: q% of p% of r
options: C. The two quantities are equal
D. The relationship cannot be determined from the information given
questions.explanation: Column A: (p/100) × (q/100) × r = pqr/10000. Column B: (q/100) × (p/100) × r = pqr/10000. Multiplication is commutative — always equal regardless of the ordering of p, q, r.
questions.trap: The ordering p < q < r is a deliberate red herring. Students think the larger percentage applied first makes a difference.

questions.question: A sum of money invested at compound interest amounts to $5,000 in 2 years and $5,500 in 3 years. What is the annual rate of interest, as a percent? Enter your answer as a number.
questions.explanation:
The insight: under compound interest every year multiplies the balance by the same factor (1 + r).
The balance goes from $5,000 at the end of year 2 to $5,500 at the end of year 3, so that factor is:
5500/5000 = 1.10
Therefore 1 + r = 1.10, and r = 0.10 = 10%.
Why the shortcut works algebraically: P(1+r)^3 / P(1+r)^2 = (1+r), and both P and the exponents cancel.
Answer: 10.
questions.trap: Setting up P(1+r)^2 = 5000 and P(1+r)^3 = 5500 as a system in two unknowns and grinding through it. Dividing one equation by the other eliminates P in one step. The other error is computing 500/5500 = 9.09%, using the END balance as the base instead of the balance the interest was earned on.

questions.question: A company's profit changed by x% in year 1 and by y% in year 2 (x and y may be negative), and the overall change over the two years was exactly +44%. Which of the following (x, y) pairs are possible? Select all that apply.
questions.trap: Every option except E has x + y within a whisker of 40, so additive reasoning cannot tell A (40) from B (40) or D (41) - and adding to the target 44 points only at C, which happens to be correct for the wrong reason. The test is the PRODUCT of the multipliers, never the sum of the percents: 1.10 x 1.30 = 1.43 and 1.20 x 1.21 = 1.452 both miss 1.44. E checks whether you will accept a negative second year, which the stem allows.

questions.question: Numbers A, B, C and D satisfy: A is 20% more than B, B is 25% less than C, and C is 60% of D. A is what percent of D?
questions.explanation:
Work from D, the base at the far end of the chain, and attach each percent to its own base.
C = 0.60D
B = C reduced by 25% = 0.75C = 0.75 x 0.60D = 0.45D
A = B increased by 20% = 1.20B = 1.20 x 0.45D = 0.54D
So A = 54% of D.
One line: 1.20 x 0.75 x 0.60 = 0.54.
Answer: 54%.
questions.trap: Adding and subtracting the percents - 60 - 25 + 20 = 55 - which is planted as choice B. Each percent is measured against a different quantity, so they cannot be combined additively. Choice E, 72%, is the second live error: chaining 1.20 x 0.60 and dropping the 25% cut entirely.
